name: Tutong 1
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired Glottolog entry, merged into Brunei Bisaya [bsb] 2008; no separate literature

sources.citation: Gardiner, Ishamina Athirah, David Deterding & Yabit Alas. 2019. The pronunciation of Dusun. Southeast Asia: A Multidisciplinary Journal 19: 14-21 (UBD FASS; open access) + companion website fass.ubd.edu.bn/research/dusun/.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Consultant is a 54-year-old male from Batang Mitus, Tutong District (the 'Tutong 1' area). Covers 18 consonants, 4 vowels, word-final diphthongs, (N)(C)V(C) syllable, long vowels analysed as bisyllabic, NWS passage with intonation arrows; the words stress/accent/prominence do not occur.

sources.note: Silent. Sec. 3 'Dusun' pp.155-156 gives the identity key: Wurm & Hattori (1983) 'treat Dusun proper (called Tutong 1) as a language different from Bisaya? (called Southern Bisaya)'; Dusun proper spoken in Belait and Tutong districts (informant Kuala Ungur); only phonetic remark is r = [r] coastal vs velar fricative inland. Swadesh lists unmarked for stress.
